clue.text: Make unsightly winter garment female abandons

indicators.note: the female walks out on the garment, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: a scarf is worn round the neck in cold weather

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a woman spoils her look by shedding her winter scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: To scar something is to mark or disfigure it, leaving it blemished and less pleasant to look at.

clue.text: Eliot initially turned up new handle or nom de plume

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the initials are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the poet T. S. Eliot's initials are T and S

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of handle are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A query about whether T. S. Eliot's initials showed up as a fresh handle, or pen name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eliot initially' is not just E: it is the initials T S, turned up to give ST. Rearranging HANDLE gives ENDHAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stendhal was the pen name of the French novelist Marie-Henri Beyle, author of The Red and the Black.

clue.text: Jerseys, say, Conservative PM once shortened

indicators.note: shortened means the surname loses its final letter

parts.note: Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: Political picture: jerseys worn by a Tory and a former prime minister, cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: Jerseys look like pullovers, but here they are the dairy breed from the Channel Island of Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerseys are a breed of dairy cow, so they are an example of farm cattle; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Slip behind yellow area with many layers

indicators.note: behind places the slip after the yellow in the answer

parts.note: yellow and chicken both mean cowardly
a run is a ladder in tights or stockings, a slip in the knit

explanation.surface: Someone slips behind a yellow patch in an area with many strata.
explanation.walkthrough: Layers suggest strata of rock or cake; they are hens that lay eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken run is an enclosure for hens, the birds that lay eggs, so it holds many layers.

clue.text: Account we hear bona fide banks cited

indicators.note: banks means the real lines both sides of the cited, like riverbanks

parts.note: bona fide means genuine, real
cit. is the scholarly abbreviation for cited, as in op. cit.

explanation.surface: A report reaches our ears that genuine banks were mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' is part of the definition, not a homophone signal: a recital is both an account and a performance we listen to.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a detailed narration of events, an account, and also a musical performance listened to by an audience.

clue.text: Deny, e.g., King Edward overthrown

indicators.note: overthrown turns the word upside down, which in a down entry reads it backwards

parts.note: King Edward is a variety of potato, an example of a tuber

explanation.surface: Someone denies that King Edward, for instance, was deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward looks like a monarch, but it is a British potato variety.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut a claim is to argue against it and refute it, which amounts to denying it.

clue.text: Line for The Apprentice, given lucre ran out

indicators.note: out means the letters of the three words are knocked out of their order and reshaped

explanation.surface: A TV quip: a contestant on The Apprentice handed money, which soon ran out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Apprentice is the business reality show, but read lower-case any apprentice is a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: A learning curve is a graph line showing how a novice's skill improves with practice, so it charts a trainee's progress.

clue.text: Maybe a grateful grandma — she stitches coats

indicators.note: coats means the words wrap around the answer, which lies within their letters

explanation.surface: A thankful grandmother, perhaps, as she sews coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grateful' is read as grate-full, what a fireplace grate holds; the def stops there and grandma begins the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: After a fire, a grate is full of cinders and powdery residue, so a grate-full is an example of these remains.

clue.text: English linesman having second to think in Paris

parts.note: penser is the French verb to think

explanation.surface: A football assistant referee from England takes a moment to think in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: A linesman sounds like a football official; here it is a writer of lines of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser, author of The Faerie Queene, was an English poet, a writer of lines of verse.

clue.text: Honour actor finally playing Shakespearean role

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word actor

parts.note: on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: An actor at last receives an honour while playing a role from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is the fairy king in A Midsummer Night's Dream, a part in a play by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Words such as a bizarre realist pens in chapter

indicators.note: pens in means encloses, so the rearranged letters hold the chapter letter
bizarre says the letters of realist are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: An odd realist writer includes something in a chapter of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' looks like a throwaway word, but it is itself an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, 'a' and 'the' are articles, the indefinite and definite determiners placed before nouns.

clue.text: Rock song then cover of Erasure for rock group

indicators.note: rock means shake about, so these letters are jolted into another order
the outside letters of the word, its first and last, wrap it like a cover

explanation.surface: Music talk: a rock song, then a cover version by the band Erasure.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'rock's mislead toward music: the first is the anagram signal, the last means stones. Erasure is a British synth-pop duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge is the prehistoric circle of standing stones on Salisbury Plain, a group of large rocks.

clue.text: Stressful moment fixing fences

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so the fixing word surrounds the moment

parts.note: nailing means fixing in place with nails
a bit is a short while, as in wait a bit

explanation.surface: A tense moment while someone is putting up fences.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail-biting situation causes anxiety and suspense, so it is tense and nerve-racking.

clue.text: Tablets picked up giving relief

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is read as it sounds

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so several are Es

explanation.surface: Taking pills to get relief from pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Tablets suggest painkillers, but they are ecstasy pills, Es, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is freedom from pain or worry, which is what relief brings.

clue.text: Show backward country gripped by fear? Thus the problem may be solved

definitions.text: Thus the problem may be solved

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the fear word

parts.note: terror is extreme fear

indicators.note: backward has the show word read from right to left

parts.note: to air something is to show it in public
a land is a country

explanation.surface: A show about a backward nation seized by fear, which might solve the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward country' looks like one phrase; backward belongs only to Show, turning AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Trial and error is the method of trying approaches repeatedly until one works, a way of reaching a solution.

clue.text: By leaving Spain, where bad driver may end up

indicators.note: leaving means the Spain letter goes out of the phrase

parts.words: where bad driver may end up
parts.note: in golf, a poorly hit drive lands in the rough, the long grass
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A careless motorist leaves Spain and ends up somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The driver is a golfer with a driver club, not a motorist; THE ROUGH loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Through and by can both mean by means of, as in 'succeeded through hard work'.

clue.text: Raised game in finale going on a long time

indicators.note: in places the raised game inside the finale

parts.note: a finale is an ending

indicators.note: raised means lifted, so in a down entry the game is read upwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A game in its final stages has been going on for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enduring lasts and persists over a long period, continuing without fading.

clue.text: Good saving returns generating interest

indicators.note: returns means the except word comes back the other way

parts.note: saving in the sense except: bar means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: Good savings make returns that earn interest.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial surface hides 'saving' as the preposition meaning except, and interest as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab someone is informal for capturing their attention, as in 'how does that grab you?'

clue.text: A Western deprived of Oscar is possibly flat

indicators.note: deprived of means the Oscar letter is taken out

parts.note: occidental means western
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Western film loses out on an Oscar and is possibly a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' sounds like dull, but in music an accidental is a sharp, flat or natural sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat sign placed before a note outside the key signature is one kind of musical accidental.

clue.text: Max, Mike and Jack hosted by a sober individual

indicators.note: hosted by means held within, so the sober pair surround the other letters

parts.note: TT is a teetotaller, someone who stays sober
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a jack is a sailor, and OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: Three men, Max, Mike and Jack, entertained by a teetotal host.
explanation.walkthrough: Max looks like a name alongside Mike and Jack; it is short for maximum.
explanation.definitionFit: Max, short for maximum, means at most, the upper limit, as in 'five people max'.

clue.text: Make up lunch now?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make amends for a wrong
second meaning: split 2,3, it is one o'clock, a usual time to eat lunch

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning needs the answer split into two words, a time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends, while at one o'clock is a typical lunchtime.

clue.text: US general stores overwhelm exhausted shopper

indicators.note: stores means keeps inside, so the general holds the emptied word

parts.note: George Armstrong Custer was a US cavalry general, of Little Bighorn fame

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A general store in America is swamped by tired shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US general stores' reads as American general stores, but the general is Custer and stores is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer is a person who buys goods from a shop, a shopper.

clue.text: Motive of crime, short of time

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the time letter is dropped

parts.note: treason is the crime of betraying one's country

explanation.surface: The motive for an offence, when someone is pressed for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is the cause or grounds for an action, its motive.

clue.text: Father's areas to keep bees, by the sound of it

indicators.note: to keep means the areas hold the bees between them

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so two areas are AA

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is taken as it is heard

parts.note: bees said aloud are Bs, two letter Bs

explanation.surface: A father's patches of land set aside for beekeeping, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Abba is the Aramaic word for father, used in the New Testament as a title for God.

clue.text: Crew from both sides of Honduras

indicators.note: both sides of asks for the two edge letters of the country's name, said in words with the joining word between them

parts.note: Honduras is the Central American country whose name supplies the two edge letters, the opening and closing ones

explanation.surface: A crew drawn from both coasts of the Central American country.
explanation.walkthrough: The edges of Honduras are not just its first and last letters: you spell out the description, which puts the word AND between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands are workers or sailors, so a ship's hands are its crew.

clue.text: Give title to book in one line I cut foolishly

indicators.note: in puts the book letter inside the rearranged letters
foolishly means the letters are arranged in a silly new order
cut means the I is chopped out of line

explanation.surface: An author ennobled after cutting a line from a book in a foolish edit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' acts only on 'line', and 'in' places book inside the jumbled result rather than linking the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the peerage, giving them a noble rank such as Lord.
